reader.requirement: At --std 85, MOVE must move the sending value to each identifier-2 left to right, evaluating identifier-1's subscript, reference modifier, function-identifier and (occurs-depending) length once, immediately before the first receiver, and each receiver's subscripting and length immediately before the move to that receiver, so that MOVE a (b) TO b, c (b) behaves as MOVE a (b) TO temp, MOVE temp TO b, MOVE temp TO c (b).
reader.edition-search: grep for EditionContext/CobolVersion/DialectLevel/DialectBehavior/ConstructRegistry in MoveBinder.cs, MoveEmitter.cs, SendingValueTemp.cs, ReceiverBracketEmitter.cs: the only hits are diagnostic reporting through ctx.Edition, the FROM-phrase function class gate (DialectLevel < 2014, file I/O FROM, not MOVE) and PictureAnalyzer's edition argument for the float-edited intermediate picture; the temp-freeze decision in BindMoveOf (targets.Count > 1, NeedsLengthFreeze, receiverEvaluationOvertakesSender) takes no edition input
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf05_02 covers subscripted sender/receivers and reference-modified sender and receiver; not exercised: an occurs-depending sender or receiver length, a function-identifier sender, edited/numeric/signed receivers and figurative/ALL senders across several receivers

probes.expected: A1: ODO sender length 2 taken once (CNT=1 after the first store does not shorten Y5's value); A2: receiver G3's ODO length is K=3 set by the earlier receiver; F1: FUNCTION REVERSE (X (1:I)) evaluated once with I=2; D1: TE (J) / EDE (J) use J=3 set by the first receiver; D2/D3 figurative and ALL literal per receiver; D4: SE (1) then J=2 then SE (2). All match.

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR2  (6.19.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: The sender is frozen into a SendingValueTemp whenever there is more than one receiver or its length needs freezing, and each receiver is identified immediately before its store in MoveEmitter; no edition arm. Refusal (class b) and later-edition (class c) probes do not apply to this general rule; the 1989 amendment's function-identifier sender was probed.

refuter.evidence: rmov1.cob at --std 85 and 2023 (rmov1-001, -002, identical): the standard's own example MOVE AE (B) TO B, CE (B) with B=2 gives M1=3 [00300] (sender frozen at AE (2)); reference-modified sender X (I:2) TO I, Y4 gives M2=4 [34  ] (modifier evaluated once); receiver Y4 (I:1) after I gives M3=3 [ab3d], Y4 (1:L) after L gives M4=2 [2 cd]; a receiving group containing its own ODO object takes its maximum length (§1985:VI.5.8.4 GR3b, which the reader's probes did not reach) M5=[5abcde]; a sending group with its own ODO object takes its current length M6=[2vw    ]; two receivers M7=[5vw   ] [2vw    ]. rmov2.cob --compile-only: N"AB", B"1", X"41" and PIC 1 refused COBOL0900 at 85. grep of DialectBehavior uses for ODO/MOVE/receiving/length found none on the MOVE path. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.19.4 GR2 'Any length evaluation or subscripting associated with identifier-2 is evaluated immediately before'; OK §1985:VI.5.8.4 GR3b 'If the group is a receiving item, the maximum length of the group will be used'.
